title: Privacy policy
lead: A short policy, because we collect very little.
body: We don't set any cookies. The only information we store directly on your device is your selected reading track, which is saved in your browser’s local storage. Tiny Analytics, the service we use to measure site traffic, stores one browser-local identifier and does not set any cookie. See Privacy Choices for a complete list of what is stored on your device.

Tiny Analytics helps us understand overall site usage, including which articles are read and approximately how many people visit. It assigns your browser a random visitor ID so it can distinguish returning visitors from new ones. This ID is not connected to your name, email address, or account.

When you view a page, basic technical information is sent, such as the page URL, referring site, screen size, language, browser hostname, and your IP address. Your IP address is transmitted in the same way it is when you visit any website.

If you select Yes or No in an article's “Was this helpful?” prompt, that response is also sent, together with the article and reading track it relates to. We only receive aggregated statistics and do not build individual visitor profiles from the browser ID.
Article icons are delivered through a public content delivery network (CDN). The CDN is not used for advertising, and we do not sell or share your data.
